causal_scheduler_fixture.general_finite_compiler: Every finite DAG has a topological ordering. Assign its events successive K values, offer every observer an opportunity at each K, and admit exactly the records attached to that event. Thus an unrestricted G-gated model reproduces every finite L trace.

scheduler_intervention.reading: A scheduler is gauge only when all physical observables and transition probabilities factor through the causal-order quotient. definitions_used.branch_G_cadence_denominator: One primitive global update interval delta_K, declared as a microscopic coordinate-time unit.
definitions_used.branch_L_cadence_denominator: One predecessor-indexed local update opportunity. This dimensionless rule imports neither global nor proper time and supplies no physical duration by itself.
definitions_used.causal_precedence: The invariant DAG relation, distinct from any total scheduler order.
global_clock_status_options: operationally nonidentified by the present data
definitions_used.local_order: Predecessor order on one observer's records.
definitions_used.logical_clock_order: A counter or topological extension consistent with causal precedence; it is not metric time.
definitions_used.message: A directed payload-preserving edge from a send record to a receipt/reflection record; it does not by itself define distance.
definitions_used.observer: A causally persistent subsystem represented here only by a local transition chain, stable record labels, and message ports; physical realization is assumed, not derived.
definitions_used.record: A typed stable memory transition in the model. No-retraction bookkeeping represents irreversibility but does not derive thermodynamic irreversibility.
definitions_used.record_equivalence: Equivalence under a shared operational discriminator and retention protocol; cross-observer equivalence is assumed.

verdict: CONTESTED PROPOSITION NARROWED/OVERTURNED BY MODEL CLASS. Unequal reunion counts exactly reject G-full and reject a delay-only explanation. They do not identify L against unrestricted G-gated or G-hidden: every finite causal record DAG admits a global topological scheduler and a gate compilation. A hidden K is gauge only if the complete dynamics and all observables are invariant under rescheduling; otherwise it is merely nonidentified and a scheduler-sensitive intervention can expose it. G-gated becomes explanatory only when an independently constrained gate law predicts multiple held-out observables.
